review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner; self-review, not independent approval
review.decision: Anchor each native claim with a bounded owned persistent hard link before submission
review.notes: Ctime adds useful observed evidence but alone is not sufficient to defeat device/inode reuse on a coarse timestamp filesystem. Keep HRW014 and every published T assertion unchanged. Before native intent publication/mutation, create and verify a private same-inode pin under the same managed filesystem, synchronize its directory, then capture final metadata and persist its exact basename. A cooperating writer never releases this reference until known terminal local cleanup; natural unlink/recreate cannot reuse the pinned inode, regardless of timestamp granularity. Pin absence/foreign/unknown metadata cannot authorize cleanup/input. Prepared/uncertain retains pins and exact payload; known accepted/refused retires only verified own pins after its claim transition, journal last. Orphan pre-intent pins are bounded, retained for operator inspection, not guessed/replayed/deleted. Limit1600 pins and existing200 intents; 128KiB reads. Unknown/invalid intent holds the channel. A valid bounded intent with a changed claim protects that exact batch/claim destination from every reclaim/rename; independent new events may still obtain fresh admission, preserving HRW009 Aonce/Bprogress. Known refused shared queue and exact uncertain publication remain explicit legitimate metadata transitions. Private cooperating-writer evidence is not atomic compare-and-unlink against an adversary replacing every anchor/journal. No real state or input.

cases.description: Persistent native claim anchors prevent identifier reuse independently of timestamp precision
cases.setup: Real private pins and intents in fixture HOME. Keep a pin while removing the original claim and recreating identical bytes with original mtime; inspect the original inode through the pin and verify the replacement cannot be that still-live inode. Include missing/foreign pin, metadata read error/zero time, known accepted/refused cleanup, uncertain restart and pin-cap controls. Preserve HRW009..014 assertions and actual RPC/spool path.
cases.action: Attempt recovery with replaced or missing anchors, settle valid terminal states, and inspect pins/claims/journal plus mutation counts.
cases.expected: Only a verified same-inode anchor can support native cleanup; original inode remains alive across process loss and cannot naturally be reused. Missing/foreign/unknown pin holds without deletion or native call. Accepted/refused closes only own references, uncertain preserves exact original input and pin; valid conflicting batches cannot overwrite protected claims or block independent fresh events. Pin count is bounded before mutation; errors never fall back or replay. No sleep, allocator-luck or relaxed cloud assertion.
